definitions.explanation: A day on which newspapers are not published or delivered. In Japan, all major newspapers observe the same rest days, typically one day per month.

examples.japanese: {明日|あした}は{休刊日|きゅうかんび}だ。
{休刊日|きゅうかんび}には{新聞|しんぶん}が{届|とど}かない。
examples.english: The newspaper doesn't come on no-publication days.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}の{新聞|しんぶん}の{休刊日|きゅうかんび}は{月|つき}に{一回|いっかい}あり、{各社|かくしゃ}{一斉|いっせい}に{休|やす}む。
examples.english: Japanese newspapers have one no-publication day per month, and all companies take the same day off.

notes:
A compound of {休刊|きゅうかん} (suspension of publication) and {日|び} (day). Refers specifically to the coordinated days when newspapers are not published.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {新聞|しんぶん}{休刊日|きゅうかんび}: newspaper holiday
- {休刊日|きゅうかんび}に{当|あ}たる: to fall on a no-publication day

CULTURAL NOTE:
In Japan, major newspapers coordinate their rest days so that all papers take the same day off, usually once a month. These are often the day after national holidays or during the New Year period. This practice is unique to Japan and reflects the newspaper industry's labor agreements.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {休刊|きゅうかん}: suspension of publication — can also mean a magazine ceasing publication entirely
- {休業日|きゅうぎょうび}: business holiday — a day when a business is closed
